title: Options, payoffs, exercise and no-arbitrage bounds

objectives.text: Derive long/short call/put terminal payoff and distinguish premium/profit, exercise style, multiplier and settlement/assignment obligations under an explicit contract.

Derive European no-dividend put-call parity and price bounds from terminal portfolio equality/dominance under stated financing/frictionless assumptions, without inferring an executable arbitrage trade.
Sum signed multi-leg expiry profits in integer cents and bridge the supplied float parser under a proved cent-grid bound.

blocks.markdown: A call grants its holder a right to buy the stated underlying at strike K; a put grants a right to sell, according to the contract's exercise and settlement terms. The writer/short side has the corresponding obligation if assigned; selling a contract does not merely collect a risk-free fee. Specify underlying/deliverable, strike, expiry, exercise window/cutoff, currency, multiplier and cash/physical settlement. Standard US equity examples often use 100 shares, but adjusted/index/other contracts differ. Our code requires an explicit synthetic multiplier and does not assume 100 globally.

For one unit at terminal underlying price S_T≥0, long call payoff=max(S_T-K,0), long put payoff=max(K-S_T,0). Short payoff is the negative of the long payoff before premium/costs. A long holder's payoff is nonnegative, but profit subtracts premium and financing/fees. At zero financing/costs, terminal profit=payoff-premium_paid; with known positive discount factor D to expiry, the financed premium's terminal cost is premium/D. Per-unit quoted premiums and contract totals differ by the multiplier. A call can finish in the money yet lose money after its premium.

American-style permits exercise during its contract window before/at expiry; European-style permits exercise at its specified expiry exercise event. These are exercise conventions, not the venue's geography. Actual cutoffs, automatic exercise, assignment, settlement reference price/date and cash/physical delivery must be read from the contract/broker. Exercise is not the same as selling the option to close. Exercising early may give up remaining option value and cause funding/delivery obligations; a terminal payoff formula is not an early-exercise strategy or instruction.

blocks.title: Positive intrinsic payoff need not recover the premium

steps.text: Synthetic long call: strike 10000 cents per unit, premium 700 per unit, multiplier 10, zero fees/financing, held to expiry.
At S_T=12000, per-unit payoff 2000 and contract payoff 20000. Premium total 7000, so profit 13000 cents.
At S_T=10500, the call is in the money by 500 per unit, payoff 5000 but profit -2000 after 7000 premium. Breakeven is 10700 per unit under these zero-cost assumptions.

At or below strike, payoff 0 and profit -7000. A naked short call receives premium but can face unbounded loss as the underlying rises in this idealized model; a short put has a large but finite per-unit terminal loss when a nonnegative underlying falls to 0.

blocks.caption: Expected lines: 8000 (0, -7000) (20000, 13000); 10000 (0, -7000) (0, -7000); 12000 (20000, 13000) (0, -7000); then (5000, -2000). These are economic terminal cash equivalents for a long held-to-expiry position with zero financing/fees, not actual delivery instructions, exercise optimization or broker settlement simulation.

blocks.markdown: The next relations are for EUROPEAN call/put on the SAME non-dividend-paying underlying, same strike/expiry/deliverable and currency. Assume nonnegative underlying, positive known risk-free discount D(0,T), enforceable payoffs, frictionless trading, divisible positions, feasible stock/option shorting and borrowing/lending at the same financing convention, with no credit/liquidity/fees/taxes/operational constraints. Actual bid/ask executable prices and funding/borrow differ. A violation in stale/mismatched marks is a diagnostic, not an authorized or risk-free executable trade.

Compare portfolio A=one European call plus a risk-free claim paying K at expiry, and B=one European put plus one underlying unit. If S_T≥K, both pay S_T; if S_T<K, both pay K. Therefore A and B have identical terminal cash equivalents max(S_T,K). Under the stated no-arbitrage/financing assumptions they have equal present value: c+K*D=p+S0, or c-p=S0-K*D. A zero-rate special case still includes K: c+K=p+S0, not c-p=S0. Dividends, early exercise and different contract terms require adjusted relations, not blind reuse.

Nonnegative payoffs imply c,p≥0. The underlying terminal value dominates call payoff, so c≤S0. A risk-free K claim dominates put payoff, so p≤K*D. Parity plus p≥0 gives c≥S0-K*D; parity plus c≥0 gives p≥K*D-S0. Thus max(0,S0-KD)≤c≤S0 and max(0,KD-S0)≤p≤KD. These are necessary no-arbitrage bounds under the stated assumptions, not a unique option-pricing model or a proof that any pair inside both ranges satisfies parity.

blocks.source:
from fractions import Fraction

def european_bounds(spot,strike,discount,call,put):
    if any(type(v) not in (int,Fraction) or not 0<=v<=1000000 for v in (spot,strike,call,put)):
        raise ValueError("expected exact bounded nonnegative per-unit prices")
    if type(discount) not in (int,Fraction) or not 0<discount<=2:
        raise ValueError("expected exact positive discount factor at most2")
    spot,strike,discount,call,put=map(Fraction,(spot,strike,discount,call,put))
    pv_strike=strike*discount
    call_range=(max(spot-pv_strike,0),spot)
    put_range=(max(pv_strike-spot,0),pv_strike)
    in_bounds=call_range[0]<=call<=call_range[1] and put_range[0]<=put<=put_range[1]
    parity_gap=call+pv_strike-put-spot
    return call_range,put_range,in_bounds,parity_gap

for call,put in [(12,7),(12,8),(2,0)]:
    cr,pr,valid,gap=european_bounds(100,100,Fraction(19,20),call,put)
    print(tuple(map(str,cr)),tuple(map(str,pr)),valid,str(gap))
# Terminal payoff identity behind parity; values are per-unit cents.
for terminal in (0,80,100,150):
    call_payoff=max(terminal-100,0);put_payoff=max(100-terminal,0)
    print(call_payoff+100 == put_payoff+terminal)

blocks.markdown: An American holder can exercise immediately, so its value cannot be below its immediate exercise payoff in the frictionless model. A European put cannot generally exercise early, and its lower bound involves discounted K, not automatically today's undiscounted intrinsic value when rates are positive. Do not substitute American intrinsic or early-exercise assumptions into European parity as an equality. An American pricing/optimal-stopping problem is taught later; this lesson does not assert a universal early-exercise decision, calendar-spread rule or Black-Scholes model.

Checking payoff identities catches sign/multiplier/strike mistakes. Checking price bounds/parity can expose inconsistent marks, discounts, dividend/style/deliverable mismatch or data timing, but passing them does not establish a fair volatility model, executable liquidity or future profitability. Negative rates can make D>1 while the stated European bounds still use positive KD; do not force discount factors below 1 without a rate assumption. No account options permissions, margin, borrowing, shorting or exercise authority is inferred from knowing these formulas.

Independent transfer: build the four-region long/short call/put payoff/profit table with a stated multiplier and financed premium. Prove parity by splitting at S_T=K without numerical examples. Construct a price pair inside both individual ranges but violating parity, then list real-world mismatches/frictions to investigate before calling it an arbitrage opportunity. Explain why European exercise style does not imply European geography or 100 share delivery.

References: [OCC/OIC contract/payoff/assignment overview](https://www.optionseducation.org/getcontentasset/8d382efb-64ba-431f-9b87-b7fc9b0916bf/50c2bc4c-a8ff-46ba-95c2-0e74752d147f/oic-options-overview-for-investors-final.pdf), [exercise style](https://www.optionseducation.org/news/what-is-the-difference-between-american-style-and), [OIC parity discussion/formula](https://www.optionseducation.org/advancedconcepts/put-call-parity), and [UT Austin European dominance bounds](https://web.ma.utexas.edu/users/mcudina/m339d-lecture-14-bounds-bull-spreads.pdf). Own equality/dominance derivation retains the strike-financing term explicitly rather than copying compressed prose.

Payoff, premium and side are separate

For a call, intrinsic=max(0,S-K); for a put, intrinsic=max(0,K-S). A BUY leg contributes (intrinsic-premium)*quantity; a SELL leg contributes its negative. Sum all legs independently for each terminal scenario. Quantity is already contracts under this synthetic rule; do not import a real-market contract multiplier or fees that are not specified.

Recover exact cents from the actual supplied parser

The public prices/strikes/premiums have at most two decimals, but the supplied starter parses them as float. This is not raw decimal preservation. Under the bounded values<=1000000, multiplying the nearest binary float by 100 leaves a value within far less than 0.5 of the true integer cents. For IEEE binary64 in this domain, input error is at most 2^-34 dollars and the product rounding error at most 2^-27 cent units, so total cent-unit error is at most 100*2^-34+2^-27<1.4e-8. Therefore round(value*100) recovers that unique integer; ties-even versus half-up is irrelevant because this recovery is not near a half-integer. Convert once, then do all intrinsic, premium, signed quantity and total operations in integer cents. This bridge is not safe for arbitrary floats or unbounded magnitudes.

Signed formatting and transfer

For BUY call K=100, premium=5, qty=2 plus SELL put K=90, premium=3, qty=1, at S=100 the call contributes -10 and the put +3, total -7.00; at S=110 total 13.00. Format the sign separately from abs(total) to avoid negative floor-division errors or negative zero. With <=10 legs and <=1000 scenarios, O(legs*scenarios) work is enough. Test both option types/sides, worthless and in-the-money legs, exact offsets and bounded cent recovery against original decimal strings. No live option action is implied.

from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math

def strategy_pnl(legs, prices):
    exact_legs = [(kind, side, round(strike * 100), quantity, round(premium * 100)) for (kind, side, strike, quantity, premium) in legs]
    lines = []
    for price in prices:
        spot = round(price * 100)
        pnl = 0
        for (kind, side, strike, quantity, premium) in exact_legs:
            intrinsic = max(0, spot - strike) if kind == 'C' else max(0, strike - spot)
            pnl += (1 if side == 'BUY' else -1) * (intrinsic - premium) * quantity
        sign = '-' if pnl < 0 else ''
        amount = abs(pnl)
        lines.append(f'{sign}{amount // 100}.{amount % 100:02d}')
    return lines

legs = [('C', 'BUY', 100.0, 2, 5.0), ('P', 'SELL', 90.0, 1, 3.0)]
print(*strategy_pnl(legs, [100.0, 110.0]), sep='\n')
